line: Crowley's account of Atu XX: the old Angel renamed, the letter Shin for Fire, and the child Horus born of the marriage.

sections.title: What Crowley says the card is
sections.line: The old title and the letter with its element. The table's triangle glyph cannot by itself separate Fire from Air; the element rests on the text. The table also has a second, unidentified Shin row (31 bis), not quoted here.

quotes.quote: The old card was called The Angel: or, The Last Judgment.
the letter Shin, which refers to Fire.

sections.title: Its path on the Tree
sections.line: The text gives no ends for this path. The table gives Key Scale path 31; the general rule is one letter to each of the twenty-two paths.

sections.title: What the card figures, in his words
sections.line: Crowley's account of the destruction by Fire, the child born of the marriage, and the flower-shaped Shin.

quotes.quote: The card therefore represented the destruction of the world by Fire.
As a result of the marriage of these two, the child Horus is born.
At the bottom of the card we see the letter Shin itself in a form suggestive of a flower;
